95-001.r: Kalidas Samman → prestigious annual arts award of the Government of Madhya Pradesh.

95-002.r: Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize → Science and Technology; named after CSIR's founder Director; given every year since 1957.

95-003.r: First Indian to get the Magsaysay Award ('Asian Nobel') → Vinoba Bhave, 1958, the first year of the award.

95-004.r: Dronacharya Award → excellence in sports coaching; bronze statue of Dronacharya, scroll of honour and cash.

95-005.r: Arjuna Award → excellence in sports. Jamnalal Bajaj Award → Gandhian values and social work; Tagore Award → cultural harmony; Moortidevi Award → literature (Bharatiya Jnanpith).

95-006.r: Arjuna Award prize money then → Rs. 3.0 lakh; given for good performance in sports at international level over four years.

95-007.r: Not a Nobel winner: H.J. Bhabha. Winners: R.N. Tagore (1913), C.V. Raman (1930), Mother Teresa (1979).

95-008.r: Bhatnagar Award → Science; B.C. Roy Award → Medicine; Dada Saheb Phalke Award → Film; Gandharva Award → Classical Art.

95-009.r: All four won the Nobel Peace Prize: Lech Walesa (1983), Desmond Tutu (1984), Yasser Arafat and Shimon Peres (1994, with Yitzhak Rabin).

95-010.r: Not an Indian citizen: Subrahmanyam Chandrasekhar, Indian-American astrophysicist (Nobel 1983). C.V. Raman, Mother Teresa, Tagore were Indian citizens.

95-011.r: Norman Borlaug → American agronomist, 'father of the Green Revolution'; Nobel Peace Prize 1970.

95-012.r: Stree Shakti Puraskar → women's courage and enterprise for betterment of women, and contribution to the nation and people; not for sports.

95-013.r: First Indian actress to receive the Padma Shri → Nargis Dutt (1958).

95-014.r: Not a Bharat Ratna: Raj Kapoor. Satyajit Ray (1992), Ustad Bismillah Khan and Lata Mangeshkar received it; Bharat Ratna instituted in 1954.

95-015.r: Not a Bharat Ratna: Pandit Jasraj. Bismillah Khan and Lata Mangeshkar got it in 2001; Pandit Ravishankar in 1999.

95-016.r: First woman to receive the Jnanpith Award → Ashapurna Devi (1976), for 'Pratham Pratishruti'.

95-017.r: Foreigner given Bharat Ratna in 1990 → Nelson Mandela, for ending apartheid in South Africa through a Gandhian-style movement.

95-019.r: Bharat Ratna (of options) → Pandit Ravi Shankar (1999); Amjad Ali Khan, Dr. Kurien and Sarvepalli Gopal were not awarded it.

95-020.r: First Bharat Ratna → 1954 (instituted 2 Jan 1954): Dr. S. Radhakrishnan, C. Rajagopalachari and C.V. Raman. Nehru was not among the first.
95-020.h: First trio = three Rs: Radhakrishnan, Rajagopalachari, Raman.

95-024.r: Not a Bharat Ratna when asked: Atal Bihari Vajpayee (got it 2015 with Madan Mohan Malviya). A.P.J. Abdul Kalam 1997; Lata Mangeshkar 2001; Satyajit Ray 1992.

95-025.r: Not a Bharat Ratna: Acharya Narendra Dev. J.R.D. Tata and Satyajit Ray → 1992; C. Subramaniam → 1998.

95-027.r: First woman to receive the Vyas Samman → Chitra Mudgal (2003), for her Hindi novel 'Avaan'.

95-028.r: Swarna Kamal and Rajat Kamal → awards in cinema for the best films.

95-029.r: First person of Indian origin to win the Booker Prize → V.S. Naipaul (1971, 'In a Free State').

95-030.r: Nobel Prizes (book answer) → Swedish Academy (Literature). Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences → Physics, Chemistry, Economics; Karolinska Institute → Medicine; Norwegian Nobel Committee → Peace.
95-030.c: Several bodies award Nobel Prizes; 'Swedish Academy' (Literature only) is just the closest option.

95-031.r: Chakradhar Fellowship → classical music; named after King Chakradhar Singh, an exponent of Tabla and Pakhawaj.

95-032.r: Maharana Pratap Award (set up 1982-83) → Rajasthan state award for excellence in sports.

95-033.r: Special Oscar (Academy Honorary Award) → Satyajit Ray, 1992, for outstanding contribution to films.

95-034.r: Bhartiya Jnanpith Award winner (of options) → Firaq Gorakhpuri, Urdu poet, 1969, for 'Gule Nagma'.

95-035.r: Wrong pair: first Indian Oscar nominee → Mother India (1957, Mehboob Khan), not Mughal-e-Azam. Correct: Keechak Vadham → first Tamil feature; Dhoop → first playback; Kagaz Ke Phool → first Cinemascope.

95-036.r: Pakistani citizen given Bharat Ratna → Khan Abdul Gaffar Khan ('Bacha Khan', 'Frontier Gandhi'), in 1987; born 1890 at Utmanzai.

95-037.r: Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan, founder of 'Khudai Khidmatgar' and 'Frontier Gandhi' → first non-Indian (Pakistani) Bharat Ratna, 1987.

95-038.r: Journalist awarded the Ramon Magsaysay Award → Arun Shourie (1982).
